articles.text: MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Liú Xiānsheng, nín hǎo, hǎo jiǔ bú jiàn.
AMERICAN REPORTER: Hello, Mr. Liú, I haven't seen you in a long time.
LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Hǎo jiǔ bú jiàn. Hěn máng ba?
MR. LIÚ: Yes, it's been a long time. Have you been busy?
MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Méiyou nàme máng, jiù shi lèi yìdiǎnr.
AMERICAN REPORTER: Not so busy, I'm just tired.
LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Zuìjìn yòu dào nǎr qù le?
MR. LIÚ: Where have you been to again lately?
MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Fújiàn. Fúzhōu fùjìn yǒu yíge hěn dàde jīngjì tèqū, wǒ zài nàr zhùle jǐtiān, juéde hěn yǒu yìsi.
AMERICAN REPORTER: Fújiàn. Near Fúzhōu there's a very large special economic zone where I stayed a few days. I found it very interesting.
LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Shì a. Zìcóng hé nǐmen dìngle hǎiyùn tiáoyuē yǐhòu, jǐge dà hǎigǎng dōu shi yuè gǎo yuè fánróng le.
MR. LIÚ: Yes. Ever since we concluded the sea transport treaty with you, our big ports have been getting more and more prosperous.
MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Bù jiù shi zhèixiē, Fúzhōu hái chūxiànle yìxiē hěn yǒu yìside shì.
AMERICAN REPORTER: Not only that, but some very interesting things have come about in Fúzhōu.
LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Nǐ shuōshuo kàn ne?
MR. LIÚ: What's that?

MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Zài jīngjì tèqū gōngzuòde Zhōngguó gōngren, tāmende shōurù bǐjiào duō, tāmen bǐjiào róngyi mǎidào zhìliàng bǐjiào hǎode xiāofèipǐn. Nín xiǎng zěnmeyàng? Zài jīngjì tèqū huì bu huì chūxiàn xīnde jiējí, zài zhèngzhìshang huì bu huì chūxiàn xīnde qíngkuàng?

AMERICAN REPORTER: Chinese workers who live in special economic zones have larger incomes, and it's easier for them to get higher quality consumer goods. What do you think: Will a new class appear in the special economic zones? Will a new political situation develop?
LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Nǐ qiānwàn bú yào nàme xiǎng.
MR. LIÚ: You mustn't think like that.
LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Qiánxiē nián, wǒmen zhǐ gǎo zhèngzhì bù gǎo jīngjì shi cuòwùde. Érqiě zhǐ gǎo zhèngzhì, zhèngzhì yě méiyou gǎohǎo ma!
MR. LIÚ: During those few years, we were mistaken to engage only in politics and not in economics. Moreover, we didn't even handle the politics well.
MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Nàme, nǐ xiǎng zhèige qíngkuàng hé shèhuìzhǔyìde gōngzī zhèngcè zhījiān bú huì yǒu shénme dà wèntí le?
AMERICAN REPORTER: So you don't think that there will be any big problems between this situation and the socialist wage policy?

LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Nǐ fàng xīn hǎo le, "duō láo duō dé" shi wǒmende zhèngcè. Zhèige zhèngcè shi bú huì gǎide. Gǎo yìtiān shèhuìzhǔyì jiù děi shíxíng yìtiān "duō láo duō dé"de zhèngcè. Zài jīngjì tèqūde gōngsī, gōngchǎng, duōbànr yǒu wàishāng cānjiā, tāmende tiáojiàn hǎo yìdiǎnr, gōngzuò xiàolǜ gāo yìdiǎnr, gōngren gōngzī duō yìdiǎnr shi yīnggāide. Qíngkuàng bú huì yánzhòngdào chūxiàn yíge xīnde jiējí.

MR. LIÚ: You can rest assured about that. "More pay for more work" is our policy, and it won't change. Socialism and the policy of "more pay for more work" must go hand in hand. Most of the companies and factories in special economic zones have foreign merchants participating. They have better facilities and higher efficiency. It's right that their workers have higher pay. The situation could never become so serious that a new class would appear.
MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Hǎojíle, xièxie nín.
AMERICAN REPORTER: Wonderful. Thank you.

LIÚ XIĀNSHENG: Bú kèqi, qǐng ni gàosu nǐde péngyoumen, dà gǎo Sìge Xiàndàihuà shi wǒmende fāngxiàng, fánróng jīngjì shi zhèige fāngxiàngde yíbùfen, shi wǒmen chángqīde zhèngcè, bú huì suíbiàn gǎide, qǐng gèfāngmiànde péngyou fàng xīn.

MR. LIÚ: Not at all. And please tell your friends that going all out with the Four Modernizations is our direction. Making our economy prosper is one part of that big direction, and it's our long-term policy. We won't change it arbitrarily. Ask our friends in all spheres to rest assured.
MĚIGUÓ JÌZHĚ: Hǎo, wǒ yídìng zhuǎngào tāmen.
AMERICAN REPORTER: All right, I'll be sure to pass the message on to them.
